threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'pavement' means walking, not a death trap with cyclists zooming by. Welcome to Hackney!
Last night on the 35, a guy argued with the driver about the time. When the driver said 'When I'm late, I'm late,' the whole bus erupted in laughter.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy juggling flaming torches while waiting for the bus at Karl-Marx-Strasse. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only here do people argue passionately over the best currywurst while standing in line for a club that hasn't even opened yet.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can name three taquerias and then argue over which one has the best salsa. The passion is real.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni at Civic Center today, and a dog hopped off the tracks just in time. Everyone paused, then erupted in laughter. Just another day in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí, but it's the dimly lit bars and late-night xurros that pulse with real local life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them easily; they're the ones taking photos of everything on Carrer Verdi while walking into oncoming traffic.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think waiting 15 minutes for a late bus is a tragedy instead of just your new normal.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded us with classic soul while the driver pretended not to hear. Felt like we were in a little Brixton concert.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the smell of fresh döner from the late-night stand mixed with sounds of kids playing on the street, I knew I’d found home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a hidden beer garden in an abandoned factory, where the sound of a local DJ sneaks through the graffiti-covered walls.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they know to avoid BART during peak hours, especially after a smoke scare at Civic Center. The bus is often no better—just a hot mess.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a suit calmly eating his lunch on a packed Muni while a street performer juggled flaming batons. Just another Tuesday in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think all the locals are night owls, but the truth is, many of us prefer a quiet evening with a good book over late-night partying.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they still look for the 'xarcuteria' sign when asking for cured meats, instead of just saying 'charcutería.'
